evidence.text: The database reports that the graph 后 is first seen in late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions with the sense ‘ruler’. It says bronze forms distinguish right-facing 后 from left-facing 司, while oracle-bone forms show no such directional distinction; it attributes the view that the two were originally one graph to Tang Lan and Li Xiaoding. It separately reports Wang Guowei’s identification of oracle 后 written with 毓. These are competing scholarly accounts, not a settled component analysis of the received graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》
evidence.text: The dictionary gives modern Mandarin hòu and separately records ‘king’, ‘feudal lord’, and ‘ruler’s principal wife’, with citations to Shijing 商頌·玄鳥, Zuozhuan 僖公三十二年, Shujing 舜典, and Han shu 景帝紀. It also records ‘later’ as a use borrowing the spelling 后 for 後, citing Liji 大學. These lexicographic citations document received-text uses but do not establish a dated semantic chain from childbirth or a body-part depiction.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：后

evidence.text: The opened search-result text says 后 and 後 were originally unrelated graphs, but homophones, and so sometimes substituted for one another in texts; it states that mainland simplified-character standards promulgated in 1964 and 1986 made 后 the simplified form of 後, thereby creating an explicit modern variant relationship. The target page did not open in this session, so these details are retained as search-result evidence rather than independently inspected page text.
evidence.title: [A01287-012] 后 (後) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 甲骨文字形 record 後1.1.5
evidence.text: This exact record page labels its specimen as 甲骨文, gives the source label 後1.1.5 and 合24440, and associates the record with the graph 後. It is therefore a candidate for 後’s oracle-bone record, not evidence for the distinct graph 后 merely because the forms/readings are similar.

search_audit.outcome: Opened returned Xiaoxuetang pages. The records are explicitly labeled 後 and carry oracle-bone source identifiers; they do not establish identity as 后, so no image candidate was selected.

gaps: The external pages inspected do not resolve the competing explanations for the earliest graphic shape of 后, including the same-graph/orientation account for 后 and 司 and Wang Guowei’s report of an oracle form written with 毓. No secure component-by-component decomposition, corruption path, childbirth depiction, or rear-body depiction is established here.

The CUHK database dates the bronze appearance to late Spring and Autumn and cites a bronze use for ‘ruler’, but this search did not verify the earliest examples against primary inscription editions or securely date the relevant oracle usages.

The Ministry lexicon provides received-text examples for ruler, lord, ruler’s wife, and later/after, but those citations do not date the transitions or demonstrate a succession-to-empress semantic chain.

The Ministry variant-dictionary result reports classical spelling substitution and 1964/1986 standardization, but its page failed to open. Classical loan chronology and the precise administrative history remain unverified from an inspected page.

No image was selected. Wikimedia Commons search results suggested reusable 後 bronze redrawings, but source pages failed to open; Xiaoxuetang results inspected were labeled 後 rather than 后, and the required specific CC0 rights notice was not verified. No artifact photograph or glyph pixels were visually inspected.

limitations.text: No usable candidate for 后 with verified identity and reuse provenance was established. Commons image-page access failed; the Xiaoxuetang candidates surfaced and inspected were specifically labeled 後, and the CC0 notice was not opened. Do not use these candidates as images for 后 based on resemblance or shared modern reading.
